groups.sentence: Administrators ensure AI tools and systems comply with accessibility standards and are accessible to all users, providing accommodations where needed.
Instructors weigh accessibility, including vendor accessibility documentation, when choosing and integrating AI tools into their courses.
Instructors coordinate with campus disability services, refer students there, and discuss assistive tool use with approved students.
Instructors apply universal design principles to their teaching and AI-supported materials.
Instructors ensure AI use does not exclude students with disabilities and provide accommodations or accessible alternatives.
Everyone completes a required accessibility review and Equally Effective Alternative Access Plan before AI tools are used.
Students using AI for accommodations work with the disability services office and their instructor; other AI uses are prohibited unless approved.
Everyone may use AI to create accessible materials, such as alt text, captions, alternative formats and screen-reader-friendly documents.
Everyone avoids relying on AI tools that are not accessible.
AI can improve accessibility and serve as an assistive technology for students with disabilities.
AI tools and their output may be inaccessible and create barriers for people with disabilities.
Everyone designs AI tools and systems to be accessible to all and to broaden access to learning materials.
Students may use AI as assistive technology or as part of an approved disability accommodation.
Accessibility rules cover the design, acquisition and use of AI systems.
